name: Chicken Jalfrezi
description: Pakistani-style chicken jalfrezi with browned chicken, a concentrated tomato masala and quickly stir-fried onion and bell peppers that retain colour and a light bite.
ingredients: 750 g boneless chicken, cut into bite-size pieces
1 tsp red chilli powder, or to taste
method: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in batches so the pieces sear instead of releasing enough moisture to steam, then transfer them to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and ginger-garlic paste to the pan and stir briefly. Add the tomatoes, cumin, chilli powder and salt and cook until the tomatoes collapse into a thick, glossy masala.

Return the chicken and any collected juices to the pan. Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is fully cooked through, adding only a small splash of water if the concentrated masala begins sticking.
Meanwhile, heat a separate wide pan well and stir-fry the sliced onion and bell peppers for a few minutes, keeping them moving so the edges soften while the centres retain some bite.

Fold the hot vegetables into the cooked chicken masala. Add the optional soy sauce only at this stage, toss over higher heat briefly and avoid prolonged cooking that would soften the peppers excessively.
Taste for salt and chilli, finish with fresh coriander and serve immediately with roti or rice.
tips: Brown the chicken in batches so it sears instead of steaming.
Keep the tomato masala thick before adding the peppers; a watery sauce will soften them too much.
Add the vegetables near the end for colour and a light bite.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate covered. Reheat until the chicken is thoroughly hot, noting that stored peppers naturally become softer.
serving: Serve immediately with chapati or plain rice.
image_alt: Pakistani chicken jalfrezi with browned chicken, thick tomato masala, onion and colourful bell peppers
image_caption: Chicken jalfrezi finished with quickly stir-fried onion and peppers so they keep colour and a light bite.
technique: Cook the chicken-tomato masala and vegetables on separate timelines. Brown chicken in batches, reduce tomatoes until thick, then stir-fry onion and peppers quickly and fold them in only at the end.
doneness_cues: Chicken should brown rather than steam during the first stage.
Tomato masala should be thick before peppers are added.
Peppers should remain bright with a slight bite.
Finished chicken must be fully cooked through.
mistakes: Crowding chicken in a small pan.
Adding peppers early and turning them soft and grey.
Adding too much soy sauce and making the dish taste salty rather than tomato-spice led.
substitutions: Use different bell-pepper colours for appearance without changing technique.
Boneless thigh can stay juicier than breast during browning.
reheating: Reheat quickly until chicken is hot; expect stored peppers to be softer than freshly cooked.
